requirements.description: Fellowships must be provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility; excellence of the researcher and the centrality of international mobility are mandatory defining features of the action.

Proposals must focus on next-generation AI agents: autonomous systems powered by large AI language models (LLMs) or large multimodal models capable of planning, utilising tools, and performing actions autonomously to achieve specified goals based on high-level instructions.

The fellowship must take the form of either a European Postdoctoral Fellowship (duration 12–24 months, researcher of any nationality, hosted in Europe or incoming to Europe) or a Global Postdoctoral Fellowship (European national or long-term resident, outgoing phase 12–24 months in non-associated Third Country plus mandatory 12-month return phase). One of these two forms is mandatory.

Proposals must address at least one of the identified key aspects of effective AI agent design: (a) robust planning, reasoning, and search mechanisms that break complex tasks into structured subgoals; (b) effective memory and state management through short-term and external long-term memory integration; or (c) integration of external tools and APIs to overcome large AI model limitations.
requirements.source_section: Scope — European Postdoctoral Fellowships / Global Postdoctoral Fellowships

requirements.description: Training activities implemented under the Postdoctoral Fellowships must integrate key transferable skills and competences common to all fields, including digital ones (e.g. generative AI), and foster Open Science, knowledge valorisation, and when applicable innovation and entrepreneurship, as well as good scientific conduct and research integrity.

A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, comprising research objectives, the researcher's training and career needs (including transferable skills, teaching, publications, and open science activities). The Plan must be submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action.

Optional secondment phases may be included within the overall fellowship duration: for European Fellowships, not exceeding half the requested duration; for Global Fellowships, not exceeding half the outgoing phase (max 3 months at the beneficiary at the start). Secondments cannot take place during the GF mandatory return phase.

An optional non-academic placement of up to 6 months may be included at the end of the project at a non-academic sector organisation established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. The placement must be an integral part of the proposal with added-value justification and is subject to evaluation.
requirements.source_section: Scope — Placements in the non-academic sector

requirements.description: ERA Fellowships under Work Programme Annex 11 provide specific support for fellowships implemented in a widening country; proposals targeting a widening country host may be designated as ERA Fellowships.
All proposals are expected to incorporate mechanisms for assessing and demonstrating progress, including qualitative and quantitative KPIs, benchmarking, and progress monitoring.
All proposals must allocate tasks for cohesion activities with the European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics (ADRA) and with the CSA GenAI4EU central Hub (HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).
Communicable results must be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
Projects must link to the resources offered by the AI Factories, including the Data Labs.
Research activities are scoped between TRL 2 (project start) and TRL 5 (project end); activities below TRL 2 or targeting TRL above 5 are outside the defined scope.

Proposals in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme must comply with Euratom-specific eligibility conditions; organisations active in nuclear research must be established in an EU Member State or a country associated to the Euratom Research and Training Programme.
Proposals should build on and reuse public results from relevant previously funded actions where possible.

Results may be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities and further deployed via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs); projects are expected to engage with this validation and deployment pathway.
Proposals should develop synergies with relevant International, European, national, or regional initiatives in AI research and deployment.

Proposals targeting one of the three priority application sectors — healthcare, advanced manufacturing, or in-vehicle autonomous driving — are preferred under the portfolio coverage exception and may receive preferential award treatment provided they pass all evaluation thresholds.
